competences: The learner identifies key facts about types of district leaders.
The learner explains the roles of district leaders using the sourced local-government materials.
languageCompetence: Learners read, write and pronounce: leader, councillor, district, local government, speaker, civic and political.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify five types of district leaders and describe the difference between election and appointment.
By the end of the lesson learners should be able to answer original source questions about district leadership.
priorKnowledge: Learners can identify district political and civic heads from Week 1.
materials: P4 SST school reference notes on district leadership
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the preceding lesson on district leadership and asks "Mention any four types of leaders.". They use the pupils' answers to connect earlier material to types of district leaders.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous Social Studies period, answer the opening question and identify leaders within their local council.

steps.stage: Development: Types of leaders in the district
steps.content: Uganda has political leaders. Uganda has civic leaders. Some leaders are voluntary leaders. Religious leaders serve worshipping communities. Cultural leaders serve traditional communities. Local political leaders are elected. Civic leaders are appointed.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Types of leaders in the district", including "Uganda has political leaders. Uganda has civic leaders." They explain the roles and ask "Mention any three examples of political leaders." to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.content: A president is a political leader. Members of Parliament are political leaders. Mayors are political leaders. Local council chairpersons are political leaders. Councillors are political leaders. Political leaders are chosen through voting.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Examples of political leaders", including "A president is a political leader. Members of Parliament are political leaders." They explain the roles and ask "How do political leaders attain leadership powers?" to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.content: Civic leaders provide social services. Civic leaders obtain positions by appointment. The CAO is a civic leader. The DEO manages district educational programmes. The DDHS supervises health centres. The district water officer distributes clean water.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Civic leaders", including "Civic leaders provide social services. Civic leaders obtain positions by appointment." They explain the roles and ask "Apart from civic leaders, mention any three other types of leaders." to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.content: Mention any four types of leaders. | Mention any three examples of political leaders. | How do political leaders attain leadership powers? | Apart from civic leaders, mention any three other types of leaders. | Apart from the CAO, mention any four other examples of civic leaders in your district.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original sourced questions, beginning with "Mention any four types of leaders." and "Mention any three examples of political leaders.". They supervise learners' written responses and check their answers against the leadership notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise independently, consult the facts in their notes and correct inaccurate answers after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher evaluates learning using "How do political leaders attain leadership powers?" and "Apart from civic leaders, mention any three other types of leaders.". They recap the source-grounded points and assign the remaining revision question for later practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state one important district-leadership duty and correct their work in their books.

assessment: Check written and oral responses to "Mention any four types of leaders.", "Mention any three examples of political leaders.", and "How do political leaders attain leadership powers?" and mark against the source material.
homework: Complete the sourced question "Apart from the CAO, mention any four other examples of civic leaders in your district." in the Social Studies book.
